Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:10:1.hebrew: מהו לסקול על ידו - של האב, כלומר: על פיו. אם אמר "קדשתי את בתי", ועדי קידושין אין באין לפנינו, וזינתה — מהו להחזיק על פיו כדין נערה המאורסה ולסוקלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:10:1.english: What is [the halakha] with regard to stoning on his account - [On the account] of the father; that is to say, based on his word. If he said, "I betrothed my daughter," and witnesses to the betrothal do not come before us, and she committed adultery — what is [the halakha as to whether] to establish [her status] based on his word according to the law of a betrothed maiden, and stone her?

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:11:1.english: When the Merciful One deems the father credible - [As it says:] “I gave my daughter to this man” (Deuteronomy 22:16).

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:11:2.english: With regard to a prohibition - To forbid her to everyone.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:11:3.hebrew: באומרת נתקדשתי - וזינתה אחר כן, שאין סוקלין אותה על פיה, ואע"פ שהחזיקה עצמה קודם הזנות בחזקת ארוסה. וטעמא מפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:11:3.english: In [the case of a woman] who says, "I was betrothed" - And she committed adultery afterward, that they do not stone her based on her [own] word, even though prior to the adultery she had established herself in the presumption of a betrothed woman. And the reason is explained as [the Gemara] proceeds:

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:12:1.hebrew: מרפסן איגרי - משברות גגין ועליות, כלומר: קשות לשומעיהן, שאינם מבינים טעמם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:12:1.english: [They] break roofs - [They] break roofs and upper stories; that is to say, they are difficult for those who hear them, who do not understand their reasoning.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:12:2.hebrew: השתא במקום שאם בא - האומר לפני האב "אני קידשתיה", אמרתי: נאמן לכנוס וכונס; אלמא, לא מחזקינן לה כל כך ע"פ האב כמקודשת שנחמיר עליה לאוסרה על זה — אמינא: סוקלין ע"פ האב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:12:2.english: Now, in a case where if [someone] comes - [Concerning] one who says before the father, “I betrothed her,” I said: He is deemed credible to marry [her], and he marries [her] — which shows that we do not, on the basis of the father, presume her to be betrothed to such an extent that we would be stringent regarding her to forbid her to this [man] — [yet] I say [that] we stone [her] on the basis of the father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:12:3.hebrew: מקום שאם בא לכנוס אינו כונס - כגון שאמרה: "נתקדשתי ואיני יודעת למי", שהחמרנו עליה לאוסרה למי שבא ואמר: "אני קידשתיה", אלמא בחזקת מקודשת היא ואין אנו יודעים למי — אינו דין שאם זינתה, סוקלים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:12:3.english: A case where if he came to marry [her] he may not marry [her] - Such as where she said: "I was betrothed, and I do not know to whom," where we were stringent upon her to forbid her to whoever came and said: "I betrothed her" — it follows that she has the presumptive status of being betrothed, and we do not know to whom — is it not logical that if she committed adultery, [the court] stones [her]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:13:1.hebrew: ולא היא וכו' - רב אסי קא מסיק למילתיה ואומר: ולא היא — אין זו קושיא למבין בטעמי שמועתי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:13:1.english: And it is not so, etc. - Rav Asi is concluding his statement and saying: "And it is not so" — this is not a difficulty for one who understands the reasoning behind my teaching.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:13:2.english: [The Merciful One] deemed the father credible - Therefore, they stone [her]:

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:13:3.hebrew: לדידה לא הימנה - ואין סוקלין, ולענין דיני נפשות לא קטלינן משום חששא. ולענין איסורא, טעמא אחרינא הוא: דשויתא לנפשה חתיכה דאיסורא, והאי לא מירתת מפני שמחפה עליו, ולגבי אב מירתת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:13:3.english: [The Merciful One] did not deem her credible - And [therefore] we do not stone [her], and with regard to capital cases, we do not execute [someone] based on [mere] suspicion. And with regard to the prohibition, it is for a different reason: because she rendered herself a forbidden entity; and this [claimant] is not afraid [to lie], because she covers for him, whereas with regard to the father, he is afraid [to lie].

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:14:1.hebrew: לטעמיה - דאמר: אין האב נאמן להחזיק את הבן ליענש על פיו — לא הוא ולא אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:14:1.english: [Follows] his reasoning - For he said: A father is not deemed credible to establish the status of the child so that neither he nor another will be punished based on his word.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:14:2.hebrew: בן ט' שנים - ביאתו ביאה, לחייב אחת מן העריות מיתה וקרבן. וכן קטנה בת ג', ביאתה ביאה, לחייב גדול הבא עליה — והיא ערוה עליו — למיתה וקרבן, אם יש עדים שהיא בת ג', וכן הקטן — והוא בן ט' שנים. אבל ע"פ האב, נאמן הוא לקרבן לשוגג:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:14:2.english: Nine years old - An act involving him is legally considered a halakhic union, to render [an adult woman among] the forbidden relations liable to capital punishment or a sin-offering. And similarly, regarding a minor girl of three [years], an act involving her is legally considered a halakhic union, to render an adult who entered into a forbidden union with her — where she constitutes a forbidden relation to him — liable to capital punishment and a sin-offering, if there are witnesses that she is three [years old], and similarly [regarding] the male minor, that he is nine years old. But based on the word of the father, he is deemed credible [only] with regard to a sin-offering for an unwitting transgression.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:14:3.english: But not for lashes - And [nor] to be punished with death if he engaged in intercourse with her intentionally.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:15:1.hebrew: בן י"ג ובת י"ב - נדריהן נדר והקדישן הקדש. ולענין עונשין של כל המצות, אם הביאו שתי שערות — סימן הוא, והרי הם גדולים לכל דבר. אבל קודם לכן, אין נדרן נדר ואין הקדישן הקדש; ואם הביאו שתי שערות, חוששין שמא שומא בעלמא הן, ואין נענשין בכך על שום עבירה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:15:1.english: A son of thirteen and a daughter of twelve - Their vows are [valid] vows and their consecrations are [valid] consecrations. And with regard to the punishments of all the mitzvot, if they produced two [pubic] hairs, it is a [valid] sign [of maturity], and behold, they are adults for all matters. However, prior to this [age], their vows are not vows and their consecrations are not consecrations; and if they produced two hairs, we suspect that they are merely [from] a mole, and they are not punished on that account for any transgression.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:1:1.hebrew: ע"מ שישתוק - כשישמע. רצה האב — ששתק בשעת שמיעה, מקודשת; לא רצה — שמיחה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:1:1.english: On the condition that [the father] will remain silent - When he hears [about it]. [The phrase] "the father wanted" [means] that he remained silent at the time of hearing, [and she is] betrothed; "he did not want" [means] that he protested.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:1:2.english: And behold, he remained silent to him - and the betrothal took effect.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:1:3.hebrew: אלא ע"מ שלא ימחה אבא - הך סיפא דקתני ״מלמדין״, לא מתוקמא כרישא בע"מ שישתוק, אלא בע"מ שלא ימחה; וכל כמה דמחי, עקר להו, שהרי לא קבע זמן למחאה. דרישא ליכא לאוקמא בהכי, דא"כ מאי ״רצה האב״? והלא יש בידו למחות לעולם, דאין כאן קידושין לעולם! ועל כרחך הכי קתני: ״על מנת שישתוק אבא״ — שתק, הרי זו מקודשת; לא שתק, אלא מיחה לאלתר, אינה מקודשת. ואם אמר ״ע"מ שלא ימחה אבא״ — מת האב עד שלא מיחה, הרי זו מקודשת, אבל כל ימי חייו אינם קידושין; מת הבן — מלמדין וכו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:1:3.english: Rather, "On the condition that [my] father will not object" - This latter clause [of the mishna], which teaches, "One instructs [the father to say that he does not want it]," cannot be established like the first clause as [referring to a case of] "On the condition that [my father] will remain silent," but rather [as referring to a case of] "On the condition that [my father] will not object"; and whenever he objects, he uproots [the betrothal], for [the son] did not set a time limit for [the] objection. For the first clause cannot be established in this manner, because if so, what is [the meaning of], "[If] the father wanted [she is betrothed]"? Behold, it is within his power to object forever, so there would never be [an effective] betrothal! And perforce, this is what [the mishna] is teaching: [If he said,] "On the condition that [my] father remains silent" — [if] he remained silent, she is betrothed; [if] he did not remain silent, but rather objected immediately, she is not betrothed. And if he said, "On the condition that [my] father will not object" — [if] the father died before he objected, she is betrothed; but all the days of his life, it is not [an effective] betrothal. [If] the son died, "One instructs [the father to say that he does not want it]," etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:2:1.hebrew: שאין אדם חוטא - בדבר שאינו נהנה ממנו, להתיר אשת איש חנם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:2:1.english: For a person does not sin - in a matter from which he derives no benefit, [so as] to permit a married woman [to marry] for nothing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:2:2.hebrew: ולא מוקמינן בתרי תנאי - לאוקמי באומר "על מנת שירצה אבא", כדקתני. ומי ששנה זו לא שנה זו. ובמשמעות לשון קמיפלגי: תנא דרישא סבר, לשון שתיקה הוא, וכיון ששתק חלו קידושין מיד; ותנא דסיפא סבר, לשון "לא ימחה" הוא, ואינם קידושין עד שימות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:2:2.english: And we do not establish [it] as [following] two tanna'im - [That is,] to establish [the mishna] as speaking of one who says, "on condition that my father consents," as it teaches. And the one who taught this [clause] did not teach that [clause]. Rather, they disagree about the connotation of the language: The tanna of the first clause holds that it is a language of silence, and since [the father] was silent, the betrothal takes effect immediately; and the tanna of the last clause holds that it is a language of "he does not protest," and it is not a betrothal until [the father] dies.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:3:1.hebrew: ומאי ע"מ שירצה ע"מ שלא ימחה - וכשקבע זמן למחאתו. הלכך, רצה האב — שעברו שלשים ולא מיחה — הרי זו מקודשת. לא רצה — שמיחה תוך שלשים — אינה מקודשת. מת האב בתוך שלשים — מקודשת, דאמרי': תו מאן מחי? מת הבן בתוך שלשים — מלמדין את האב כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:3:1.english: And what is "on the condition that he wants"? "On the condition that he will not object" - And [this is a case] where he set a time limit for his objection. Therefore, [if] "the father wanted" — [meaning] that thirty [days] passed and he did not object — she is betrothed. [If] "he did not want" — [meaning] that he objected within thirty [days] — she is not betrothed. [If] the father died within thirty [days], [she is] betrothed, for we say: Who can object anymore? [If] the son died within thirty [days], "one instructs the father, etc."

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:4:1.english: Both give a bill of divorce - In order to permit her to [marry] others.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:4:2.hebrew: קדשתי את בתי - קטנה, והוא לא ידע למי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:4:2.english: I betrothed my daughter - [She was] a minor, and he did not know to whom [he betrothed her]:

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:4:3.english: Both give a bill of divorce - To permit her to others.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:5:1.hebrew: אמר רב - הא דתנן: ״בא אחד ואמר: ׳אני קידשתיה׳ — נאמן״, ליתן גט קאמר דנאמן, וסמכינן עליה שהוא קידשה, וגיטו גט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:5:1.english: Rav said - That which we learned in the Mishnah: "[If] one came and said, 'I betrothed her,' he is deemed credible" — [Rav] is saying that he is deemed credible to give a bill of divorce, and we rely upon him that he betrothed her, and his bill of divorce is a [valid] bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:5:2.hebrew: נאמן לכנוס - דמירתת, דאב ודאי לא יחפה עליו. אבל האשה שקבלה קידושין ואינה יודעת ממי, ובא אחד כו' — לא מירתת, דיודע הוא שתהא מחפה עליו, ותתרצה בו, ותכחיש את כל הבא לומר עוד ״אני הוא״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:5:2.english: [He is] deemed credible to marry [her] - For he is afraid [to make a false claim], as the father certainly will not cover for him. But [in the case of] a woman who accepted betrothal and does not know from whom, and one [man] came [forward,] etc. — he is not afraid, as he knows that she will cover for him, and will be pleased with him, and will contradict anyone else who comes further to say, "I am the one."

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:5:3.hebrew: שאין אדם חוטא - בדבר שאינו נהנה ממנו, להתיר אשת איש חנם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:5:3.english: For a person does not sin - in a matter from which he derives no benefit, [namely,] to permit a married woman for nothing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:6:1.hebrew: אף נאמן לכנוס - דלא חציף למימר לפני האב שקבל הקידושין ״אני הוא״, דמירתת דלמא מכחיש ליה ואמר: ״ידענא דלאו את יהבת לי קידושין״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:6:1.english: [He is] even deemed credible to marry [her] - For [a person] is not impudent [enough] to say in the presence of the father who received the betrothal, “I am he,” since he is afraid lest [the father] contradict him and say, “I know that it was not you who gave me the betrothal [money].”

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:7:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא אחר בהדיה - שאומר "אני קדשתיה" — מירתת מעיקרא, שמא יכיר האב שחבירו קידשה ולא הוא, והאי קושטא אמר; ושכנגדו שכיחש, ירא לכונסה ונותן גט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:7:1.english: Since there is another with him - who says, "I betrothed her," [each one] is afraid from the outset lest the father recognize that his fellow betrothed her and not him, and [that] this [other one] spoke the truth; and his counterpart who lied is afraid to marry her, and gives a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:8:1.hebrew: קדשתי את בתי - קטנה, והוא לא ידע למי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:8:1.english: I betrothed my daughter - [When she was a] minor, and he did not know to whom [he had betrothed her].

Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:8:2.hebrew: נאמן לכנוס - דמירתת, דאב ודאי לא יחפה עליו. אבל האשה שקבלה קידושין ואינה יודעת ממי, ובא אחד כו' — לא מירתת, דיודע הוא שתהא מחפה עליו, ותתרצה בו, ותכחיש את כל הבא לומר עוד "אני הוא":
Rashi on Kiddushin 63b:8:2.english: Deemed credible to marry [her] - Because he is afraid [to lie], for the father certainly will not cover for him. However, [in the case of] a woman who received betrothal and does not know from whom, and one came [forward, etc.] — he is not afraid, for he knows that she will cover for him, and will be pleased with him, and will contradict anyone [else] who comes further to say: "It is I."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:11:1.hebrew: לקטלא לא הימניה - וא"ת: והא כתיב באותה פרשה דאמר "בתי נתתי לאיש הזה", ו"סקלוה" — אלמא לקטלא נמי הימניה רחמנא?! וי"ל: ד"סקלוה" מיירי היכא דאיכא עדים; מיהו לאיסורא הימניה רחמנא, כדכתיב "את בתי נתתי לאיש":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:11:1.english: With regard to execution, [the Merciful One] did not deem him credible - And if you say: But isn't it written in that [same] passage that he says, "I gave my daughter to this man" (Deuteronomy 22:16), and "and they shall stone her" (ibid. 22:21) — evidently, with regard to execution as well, the Merciful One deemed him credible?! And one can say: "And they shall stone her" deals with [a case] where there are witnesses; however, regarding the prohibition, the Merciful One deemed him credible, as it is written: "I gave my daughter to the man" (ibid. 22:16).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:14:1.hebrew: [ולא לעונשין - תימה: היכי מייתי דרב חסדא לטעמיה? הא מסתמא רב אסי לא פליג אמתניתין דלקמן, דאשבויה לא הימנו, ולמכות ולעונשין אין להאמינו טפי משבויה]: ת"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:14:1.english: ["And not with regard to punishments" - It is astounding: How can [the Gemara] cite Rav Ḥisda [as following] his [own] line of reasoning? For presumably Rav Asi does not disagree with the Mishnah below, that regarding a captive woman [the father] is not deemed credible, and with regard to lashes and punishments one should not deem him credible more than regarding a captive!]: Tosafot Yeshanim.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:15:1.hebrew: בני זה בן י"ג שנה ויום אחד - פי' בקונט': דמיירי שהביא ב' שערות, ואפ"ה צריכין אנו לידע שנותיו — שהרי שנים בלא שערות אין מועילין עד ל"ו שנה, דהיינו רוב שנותיו, וסימנים בלא שנים, דהיינו לפני י"ג, שומא נינהו; ואעפ"כ קאמר הכא גמרא דלמכות ועונשים אינו נאמן. פי': דלמכות — היכא דלא התרו בו, ולעונשין — היכא דהתרו בו. וקשה: דא"כ, כל הנשים הבאות לפנינו לחלוץ — היאך יחלוצו? אע"ג שיש להם סימנים, כיון שאין אנו יודעים שנותיהם, לא מהני, דשמא היבם קטן, ואיש כתיב בפרשה, דמשמע: ולא קטן! וכל האנשים הבאים על העריות — היאך הן נהרגים? ואע"ג שיש להם שערות, מ"מ אין אנו יודעים שנותיהן, ושמא הם קטנים! ואור"י: דאי איכא ריבוי שערות, סמכינן אריבוי שערות, דאין דרכם לבא קודם י"ג שנה; אי נמי, אם הם גדולים בקומה, יש לסמוך על הסימנים והקומה, ואפי' אין לו כי אם ב' שערות. אבל הכא מיירי שלא הביא רק ב' שערות ולא הגדיל בקומה, ולכך קאמר גמרא דלמכות ועונשין אינו נאמן. עוד פר"י שיטה אחרת: דבמקום סימנין, א"צ עדות שנים. וא"ת: א"כ, מה אנו צריכין לנאמנותו של אביו? וי"ל: דמיירי הכא שאביו העיד שכבר עבר שנה או שנתים שאכל בנו חלב או בא על הערוה, והיה גדול כשעשה את העבירות, אבל אין אנו יודעים אם היו לו שנים באותו הזמן או סימנים; ובא לאשמעינן דהאב נאמן לומר דאותו הזמן היו לו שנים או סימנים, דהיינו שתי שערות; והא דלא חשיב סימנין — חד מינייהו נקט:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:15:1.english: "This son of mine is thirteen years and one day old" - Rashi explained in the Commentary that this is dealing with [a son] who has produced two [pubic] hairs; and even so, we still need to know his years [of age], for years without hairs are of no effect until thirty-six years — which is the majority of his years [of a typical seventy-year lifespan] — and [physical] signs without years — that is, before thirteen — are merely a mole. And nevertheless, the Gemara states here that for lashes and punishments, he [the father] is not believed. Explanation: "For lashes" [refers to a case] where they did not formally warn him [of capital punishment or karet], and "for punishments" [refers to a case] where they warned him. And this is difficult: For if so, all the women who come before us to perform ḥalitzah — how could they perform ḥalitzah? Even though they have [physical] signs, since we do not know their years, it should not be effective, for perhaps the yavam is a minor, and "a man" is written in the passage (Deut. 25:7), which implies: and not a minor! And all the men who engage in forbidden sexual relations — how are they executed? For even though they have hairs, nevertheless we do not know their years, and perhaps they are minors! And the Ri says: If there is an abundance of hairs, we rely on the abundance of hairs, as it is not their usual way to come before thirteen years. Alternatively, if they are tall in stature, one may rely on the signs and the stature, even if he has no more than two hairs. Here, however, we are dealing with [a case where] he produced only two hairs and did not grow in stature; and therefore the Gemara states that for lashes and punishments, he [the father] is not believed. The Ri further explained another approach: In the presence of [physical] signs, testimony of years is not needed. And if you say: If so, why do we need the credibility of his father? And one can say: Here we are dealing with [a case where] his father testified that a year or two have already passed since his son ate [forbidden] fat or engaged in forbidden sexual relations, and that he was an adult when he committed the transgressions; but we do not know whether he had [the requisite] years at that time or [the requisite] signs. And it comes to teach us that the father is believed to state that at that time he had [the requisite] years or signs — namely, two hairs; and as for [the baraita] not mentioning signs — it mentioned one of them.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:1:1.hebrew: אלא ע"מ שישתוק אבא - פירש בקונטרס: שישתוק בשעת שמיעה. ואין לפרש: שישתוק לעולם, דא"כ היינו "שלא ימחה" דבסמוך, והיכי אמר בהם "רצה האב מקודשת", והרי שמא ימחה אח"כ ויבטל הקידושין?! אלא ש"מ: שישתוק בשעת שמיעה קאמר. וה"פ דמתני': "רצה האב" — כלומר, ששתק בשעת שמיעה — "מקודשת"; "לא רצה האב" — אלא מיחה — "אינה מקודשת"; "מת האב מקודשת" — פי': מת האב קודם השמיעה, דאין לומר אחר השמיעה ושתק ולא מיחה, דאין זה חידוש. וא"ת: מאחר דמת קודם השמיעה, היאך היא מקודשת? דלמא אי הוה שמע הוה מוחה! וי"ל: דיש לנו לדון דעתו שלא ימחה. וא"ת: אם כן, מאי פריך: "והא לא אמר אין"? אמאי לא אמרי': דעתו היה לומר אין אם הוה שמע, כדצריכינן למימר גבי שתיקה, כדפי'? ואומר ר"מ: דיש לחלק בין היכא דמחוסר אמירה, להיכא דלא מחוסר אלא שתיקה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:1:1.english: Rather, "on the condition that Father remains silent" - Rashi explained: That he remain silent at the time of hearing. And one should not explain that he remain silent forever, because if so, that is [the same as] "that he will not object" in the adjacent clause; and [furthermore], how could it say regarding them: "If the father wanted, she is betrothed" — surely perhaps he will object afterward and void the betrothal?! Rather, deduce from this that it means he remain silent at the time of hearing. And this is the explanation of the Mishnah: "If the father wanted" — that is to say, that he remained silent at the time of hearing — "she is betrothed"; "if the father did not want," but rather objected, "she is not betrothed"; "if the father died, she is betrothed" — explanation: the father died before the hearing, for one cannot say [it means he died] after the hearing and remained silent and did not object, as that is no novelty. And if you should say: Since he died before the hearing, how is she betrothed? Perhaps had he heard, he would have objected! And one can say: We must evaluate his mindset [as being] that he would not have objected. And if you should say: If so, why did [the Gemara] object: "But he did not say 'yes'"? Why do we not say that his mindset was to say "yes" had he heard, just as we must say regarding silence, as we explained? And Rabbeinu Meir says: One can distinguish between where saying [something] is lacking and where nothing is lacking except silence.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:1:2.hebrew: [והא שתיק - וליכא למימר: "מלמדין האב" היינו קודם שמיעה, שמלמדין משמע לאחר שמיעה; להכי פריך: "והא שתיק", ומאי אהני ליה תו אחרי כן]: ת"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:1:2.english: ["After all, he remained silent" - And it cannot be said that "one instructs the father" means prior to [his] hearing, for "one instructs" implies after [his] hearing; for this [reason], [the Gemara] asks: "After all, he remained silent," and what would it avail him anymore after that?]: Tosafot Yeshanim.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:1:3.hebrew: אלא ע"מ שישתוק אבא - פירש בקונטרס: שישתוק בשעת שמיעה. ואין לפרש שישתוק לעולם, דא"כ היינו "שלא ימחה" דבסמוך, והיכי אמר בהם "רצה האב מקודשת"? והרי שמא ימחה אח"כ ויבטל הקידושין! אלא ש"מ "שישתוק בשעת שמיעה" קאמר. וה"פ דמתני': "רצה האב" — כלומר, ששתק בשעת שמיעה — מקודשת; "לא רצה האב" — אלא מיחה — אינה מקודשת; "מת האב מקודשת" — פי': מת האב קודם השמיעה, דאין לומר אחר השמיעה ושתק ולא מיחה, דאין זה חידוש. וא"ת: מאחר דמת קודם השמיעה, היאך היא מקודשת? דלמא אי הוה שמע הוה מוחה! וי"ל: דיש לנו לדון דעתו שלא ימחה. וא"ת: אם כן, מאי פריך "והא לא אמר אין"? אמאי לא אמרי' דעתו היה לומר אין אם הוה שמע, כדצריכינן למימר גבי שתיקה, כדפי'? ואומר ר"מ: דיש לחלק בין היכא דמחוסר אמירה להיכא דלא מחוסר אלא שתיקה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:1:3.english: Rather, on the condition that my father will remain silent - Rashi explained: That he will remain silent at the time of hearing [about the betrothal]. And one cannot explain that [it means] he will remain silent forever, as if so, that would be [identical to the condition] "that [my father] will not object," which is [introduced] immediately following; and how could [the Mishnah] say regarding it: "If the father wanted, she is betrothed"? For perhaps he will object later and nullify the betrothal! Rather, conclude from this that [the Gemara] means: "that he will remain silent at the time of hearing." And this is the explanation of the Mishnah: "If the father wanted" — meaning that he remained silent at the time of hearing — "she is betrothed"; "If the father did not want" — but rather objected — "she is not betrothed"; "If the father died, she is betrothed" — explanation: the father died prior to the hearing, as one cannot say [that it means he died] after the hearing and had remained silent and did not object, for that is no novelty. And if you say: Since he died prior to the hearing, how is she betrothed? Perhaps had he heard, he would have objected! And one can say: We are to assess his intention that he would not object. And if you say: If so, what is the objection [that the Gemara raised]: "And behold, he did not say yes"? Why do we not say [there too that] his intention was to say yes had he heard, just as we must say regarding silence, as we explained? And Rabbeinu Meir says: One can distinguish between where an [explicit] statement is lacking, and where nothing is lacking other than silence.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:2:1.hebrew: [ולא מוקמינן בתרי תנאי - דלא כר"י בפרק המפקיד גבי חבית]: ת"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:2:1.english: ["And we do not establish [a mishna] as [following] two tanna’im" - This is not in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan in the chapter [entitled] HaMafkid regarding the barrel]: Tosafot Yeshanim.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:7:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא חד בהדיה ארתותי מירתת - ואע"ג דע"כ איכא חד מינייהו דמשקר, מיהו אותו שכיחש מתיירא לכונסה ונותן גט:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63b:7:1.english: "Since there is [another] one with him, he is afraid" - And even though perforce one of them is lying, nevertheless, the one who lied is afraid to marry her and gives a bill of divorce.
